questions.stem: On the study group revision, a turnaround typically spans how many bars?
questions.explanation: A turnaround typically spans two bars. The tempting wrong count gives four bars.

questions.stem: On the study group revision, the dominant scale is mixolydian with what change?

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The section form of a rhythm change
questions.learningObjective: State the section form of a rhythm change
questions.stem: On the study group revision, what are the four sections of a rhythm change?

answer.exemplar: The four sections are A, A, B, and A, forming the classic AABA thirty-two-bar form.

questions.explanation: The sections are A, A, B, A. The tempting wrong idea gives A, B, A, B.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The total length of a rhythm change
questions.learningObjective: Compute the total length of a rhythm change
questions.stem: On the study group revision, four sections of eight bars each make how many bars total?
questions.explanation: Four times eight is thirty-two bars. The tempting wrong count gives twenty-four bars.
questions.hint: Multiply sections by bars per section.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Modal interchange and the chords it borrows
questions.learningObjective: State what modal interchange borrows
questions.stem: On the study group revision, modal interchange in a major key can borrow which chord?

options.text: The vii chord from the relative minor
The I chord from the same key
The V chord from the dominant key
The iv chord from the parallel minor

questions.explanation: Modal interchange can borrow the iv chord from the parallel minor. The tempting wrong idea borrows from the dominant key.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: How many notes a borrowed chord adds
questions.learningObjective: Count notes a borrowed chord adds

stimulus.body: The study group borrows a bVI chord in a major key, introducing notes not in the original major scale.

questions.stem: How many notes does that borrowed bVI chord introduce outside the major key?

options.text: Three notes, adding the flattened seventh
Two notes, the flattened third and sixth

questions.explanation: A borrowed bVI introduces one note outside the key, the flattened sixth. The tempting wrong idea adds the flattened third.
questions.hint: Compare borrowed chord tones to the key.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The distance to an altered thirteenth
questions.learningObjective: Measure the distance to an altered thirteenth
questions.stem: On the study group revision, how many semitones separate an altered thirteenth from the root?

answer.exemplar: An altered thirteenth sits twenty-one semitones above the root, with its quality raised or lowered from the natural thirteenth.

questions.explanation: A thirteenth is twenty-one semitones above the root. The tempting wrong idea counts fourteen semitones.

questions.topic: The distance between a dominant and its tritone substitute

questions.stem: On the study group revision, how many semitones separate a dominant root from its tritone substitute root?
